This confirms `GHUser.wrap(users, root)` already existed as a utility method at the time (used elsewhere, e.g. `followers`), and similar `PagedIterator` patterns elsewhere (e.g. events) correctly call a wrap-up on each item. The commit a23d6f6 introduced the new `PagedIterable`/`PagedIterator`-based `getMembers()` but left `wrapUp` empty, failing to call `GHUser.wrap(users, root)` — exactly the omission later fixed in 8fb3177.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a23d6f60d57fab770e036948efe7f5973cedffb1

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I traced the history of `src/main/java/org/kohsuke/github/GHOrganization.java` with `git log --follow -p`, searching for when the `PagedIterator<GHUser> ... wrapUp(GHUser[] ...)` pattern (the exact code touched by the fix) first appeared.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `a23d6f6` (Ryan Kennedy, "refactor getMembers to use PagedIterable") replaced the old `getMembers()` implementation — an `AbstractList<GHUser>` that resolved each user via `root.getUser(shallow[index].getLogin())`, i.e., a real round-trip that produced fully-wired `GHUser` objects — with a new `PagedIterable<GHUser>`/`PagedIterator<GHUser>` implementation. In the refactor, the `wrapUp(GHUser[] page)` override was left as an **empty body**, so the `root` field (and other wiring normally done by `GHUser.wrap`) was never set on the paged results. Subsequent commits (`2555620`, `e97fd9c`) extended this method (adding filter params, renaming to a shared `suffix`/`listMembers` helper for both members and public-members) but always preserved the same empty `wrapUp` body, carrying the bug forward unchanged.

**(3) Evidence:** 
- `git show a23d6f6` shows the empty `wrapUp(GHUser[] page) { }` being introduced for the first time in this exact spot.
- `GHUser.wrap(GHUser[] users, GitHub root)` already existed in `GHUser.java` at that point and was used by sibling methods (e.g., `getFollowers()`), showing the expected pattern that was simply omitted here.
- The bug-fixing commit `8fb3177` only adds the single missing line `GHUser.wrap(users, root);` inside that same `wrapUp` override — a direct, minimal fix of the omission from `a23d6f6`.
- Intermediate commits `2555620` and `e97fd9c` modified surrounding code (filter parameter, suffix generalization) but never touched/fixed the empty `wrapUp` body, confirming they just carried the pre-existing bug forward rather than introducing it.

I'm confident in this attribution — the fix diff maps precisely onto the empty method body first created in `a23d6f6`, and no other commit in the file's history touches that line until the fix itself.
